label: Residents 16 to 24
desc: Residents aged 16 to 24 — ACS 2020–24 estimate (table B23001). The Summer Youth Employment Program takes 14- to 24-year-olds; the survey's work and poverty data for small areas start at 16, so 16 to 24 is the band used throughout this map.

label: Share aged 16 to 24
desc: Share of residents aged 16 to 24 — ACS 2020–24 estimate.

label: Residents 16 to 24 per square mile
desc: Residents aged 16 to 24 per square mile of land.

label: Residents 14 to 24 (2020 count)
desc: Residents aged 14 to 24, the program's full eligible range, from the 2020 census (single years of age, table PCT12). A count rather than a survey estimate, but six years old. The Census Bureau adds small random noise to protect privacy, so very small areas can be off by a few people.

label: Children under 18
desc: Residents younger than 18 — ACS 2020–24 estimate.

label: Residents under 25
desc: Residents aged 24 and younger — ACS 2020–24 estimate.

label: Share under 25
desc: Share of residents aged 24 and younger — ACS 2020–24 estimate.

label: Poverty rate, ages 16 to 24
desc: Share of residents 16 to 24 below the federal poverty line, among those whose poverty status is determined (ACS B17001). Students living in college dorms are outside the survey's poverty count.

label: Child poverty rate
desc: Share of children under 18 below the federal poverty line, among those whose poverty status is determined (ACS B17001).

label: Unemployment rate, ages 16 to 24
desc: Unemployed residents 16 to 24 as a share of those in the civilian labor force, meaning working or looking for work (ACS B23001).

label: Teens 16 to 19 not in school or working
desc: Share of 16- to 19-year-olds who are neither enrolled in school nor employed (ACS B14005), often called disconnected or opportunity youth. For small areas the Census Bureau publishes this measure only for ages 16 to 19.

label: Young adults 18 to 24 without a diploma
desc: Share of residents 18 to 24 whose schooling stopped short of a high school diploma or equivalency (ACS B15001). Includes some 18-year-olds still in high school.

label: Arrests under 25, per 1,000 residents 10 to 24
desc: NYPD arrests of people 24 and younger in 2024 (the under-18 and 18-to-24 groups combined) per 1,000 residents aged 10 to 24. NYPD records age only in bands, so 24 and younger is the closest cut to "under 24". Counted where the arrest was made. The precinct view counts every arrest; the neighborhood view leaves out the quarter NYPD logged at a precinct station house. See the under-18 count for the caveats. Not shown where fewer than 100 residents are 10 to 24.
source: NYPD arrest data, 2024 (8h9b-rp9u); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Arrests under 25 (count)
desc: NYPD arrests of people 24 and younger in calendar 2024, in NYPD's own patrol, transit and housing jurisdictions: the under-18 and 18-to-24 counts added together, with the same placement rules and caveats.
source: NYPD arrest data, 2024 (8h9b-rp9u); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Arrests under 18, per 1,000 residents 10 to 17
desc: NYPD arrests of people under 18 in 2024 per 1,000 residents aged 10 to 17. The arrest is counted where it was made and the residents where they live, so places that draw young people from elsewhere, such as shopping strips and transit hubs, run high. Not shown where fewer than 100 residents are 10 to 17. See the count for the caveats on 2024 and on station-house arrests.
source: NYPD arrest data, 2024 (8h9b-rp9u); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Arrests under 18 (count)
desc: NYPD arrests of people under 18 in calendar 2024, in NYPD's own patrol, transit and housing jurisdictions, placed where the arrest was made. 2024 is the latest full year in which NYPD's file records an age for nearly every arrest; the 2025 file has no age on 53% of arrests. NYPD logged a third of 2024 under-18 arrests at the precinct station house because it had no street location for them (footnote 6 of NYPD's arrest data). The precinct view counts them, by the precinct NYPD assigned. The neighborhood view leaves them out, so its counts understate, by more in precincts that log more arrests that way (from 15% to 44% of youth arrests), and splits an arrest whose street point sits on a boundary equally between the areas that meet there. Arrests reflect police activity as well as offending, and where someone is arrested is not where they live.
source: NYPD arrest data, 2024 (8h9b-rp9u); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Arrests ages 18 to 24, per 1,000 residents 18 to 24
desc: NYPD arrests of people aged 18 to 24 in 2024 per 1,000 residents aged 18 to 24. Same caveats as the under-18 rate. Not shown where fewer than 100 residents are 18 to 24.
source: NYPD arrest data, 2024 (8h9b-rp9u); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Arrests ages 18 to 24 (count)
desc: NYPD arrests of people aged 18 to 24 in calendar 2024, placed where the arrest was made. Arrests NYPD logged at a precinct station house (23% of this age group) count in the precinct view and are left out of the neighborhood view, as described for the under-18 count.
source: NYPD arrest data, 2024 (8h9b-rp9u); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Shooting victims under 25, per 10,000 residents under 25 a year
desc: People under 25 shot in the area, July 2023 through June 2026, as a yearly average per 10,000 residents under 25 (NYPD shooting victims). Counted where the shooting happened, not where the victim lived.
source: NYPD shooting incidents, offenders and victims (5ucz-vwe8, gdk4-mbsv, pztn-9bne); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Shooting victims under 25 (count, 3 years)
desc: People under 25 shot from July 2023 through June 2026, placed where the shooting happened (NYPD shooting incidents and victims). NYPD logs about one in eight of these shootings at the precinct station house, without a street location; the precinct view counts them and the neighborhood view leaves them out.
source: NYPD shooting incidents, offenders and victims (5ucz-vwe8, gdk4-mbsv, pztn-9bne); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Shootings with a suspect under 25, per 10,000 residents a year
desc: Shooting incidents with at least one suspect under 25, July 2023 through June 2026, as a yearly average per 10,000 residents. NYPD lists no suspect for about two in five shootings, so this undercounts.
source: NYPD shooting incidents, offenders and victims (5ucz-vwe8, gdk4-mbsv, pztn-9bne); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Shootings with a suspect under 25 (count, 3 years)
desc: Shooting incidents from July 2023 through June 2026 in which NYPD lists at least one suspect under 25, placed where the shooting happened; the one in nine that NYPD logged at the precinct station house, without a street location, count in the precinct view and are left out of the neighborhood view. A suspect is someone NYPD identified or described, not necessarily someone arrested or convicted.
source: NYPD shooting incidents, offenders and victims (5ucz-vwe8, gdk4-mbsv, pztn-9bne); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Violent crimes against people under 25, per 1,000 residents under 25
desc: Murders, robberies and felony assaults with a victim under 25, July 2025 through June 2026, per 1,000 residents under 25. Counted where the crime happened. See the count for what is included.
source: NYPD complaint data (Historic + Year-to-Date); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Violent crimes against people under 25 (count)
desc: Murders, robberies and felony assaults reported to NYPD from July 2025 through June 2026 in which the victim was under 25, by report date. Rape is left out because NYPD records nearly every rape complaint at the precinct station house to protect victims. About 5% of these complaints carry no victim age and are not counted. The 2% that NYPD logged at the precinct station house, without a street location, count in the precinct view and are left out of the neighborhood view.
source: NYPD complaint data (Historic + Year-to-Date); residents from ACS 2020–24

label: Summer jobs sites within a mile
desc: Summer Youth Employment Program sites within one mile of where the area's young people live: counted from each census tract's internal point (a point inside the tract near its middle), then averaged across the area's tracts weighted by residents 16 to 24, so it reflects what a typical young resident has nearby. Sites are summer 2025 locations from the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD): where provider organizations enroll and serve participants, one entry per location, year-round programs excluded.
